clue.text: New lease negotiated to include game, which is instrumental in a funny way

definitions.text: which is instrumental in a funny way

indicators.note: the reshuffled letters take in the game, holding it within them
terms that are negotiated get worked over and rearranged, so the letters of new lease are reshuffled

parts.note: whist is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: A tenant haggles over a renewed lease that bundles in some sporting rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' makes SWANEELE; 'game' is a card game, not a quarry. A swanee whistle is a toy slide whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: A slide whistle with a plunger makes comic swooping notes, so it is a musical instrument used for laughs.

clue.text: I can't hear you drink outside Crown

indicators.note: the drink goes round the outside of the summit

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a crown is the top or peak of something

explanation.surface: A drinker in a noisy Crown pub shouts back at a mumbling friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' suggests a pub name or royalty; here it is a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who can't hear you asks you to talk louder, the idiom being the request itself.

clue.text: Ace spaceman humming with excitement?

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
Buzz Aldrin was an Apollo 11 astronaut

explanation.surface: A top astronaut thrilled and buzzing at launch.
explanation.definitionFit: A place full of excited chatter is said to be buzzing, filled with excitement.

clue.text: You mock spoken speech hesitancy as a music-maker

indicators.note: said out loud, the two words run together into one sound

parts.note: you plus phoney, mock meaning fake
um is the filler noise of a hesitant speaker

explanation.surface: A heckler mocks a stammering musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mock' is an adjective, fake, not the verb it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: This brass instrument is a small tuba, so it makes music.

clue.text: See 1
Chicory's the thing, with length covered in bark

indicators.note: the pronoun and letter are wrapped inside the dog's bark

parts.note: woof is a dog's bark
it, as in that's it, the very thing

explanation.surface: Chicory is the ideal choice, long and wrapped in tree bark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' suggests a tree, but it is a dog's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Witloof is the Belgian chicory grown blanched for its tight leaf heads.

clue.text: Hair woven on masculine religious garment

indicators.note: woven strands are intertwined, so the letters of hair are rearranged

parts.note: M is the grammatical abbreviation for masculine

explanation.surface: A man's holy robe woven from hair, like a hair shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Muslim pilgrims to Mecca wear this white seamless garment as a sacred dress.

clue.text: Bananas, both with a blue Mediterranean salad dish

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe of bananas plus something blue for a Mediterranean salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like an ingredient but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This Levantine salad of bulgur, parsley and mint is served across the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Model on road: wow, in tailored set!

indicators.note: the exclamation goes inside the rearranged letters
something tailored is cut and reshaped, so set is rearranged

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like wow

explanation.surface: A fashion model on the street in a sharp suit draws gasps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailored' gives EST. 'Model' suggests a person, but it is a car model; COR is a British cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ford Escort was a long-running popular car model.

clue.text: Appendage of quality that is a monstrous thing

parts.note: -ness is a suffix forming nouns of quality, as in boldness
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: An extra flourish of quality turns out monstrous.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the pet name of the Loch Ness Monster, a legendary Scottish lake creature.

clue.text: Sally cosies up to blokes in alien gear

indicators.note: the pair sits inside the alien's letters

parts.note: ET is the film extraterrestrial, a standard crossword alien

indicators.note: snuggling up beside means the first piece sits right next to the second

parts.note: a sally is a witty retort, a quip
blokes are men

explanation.surface: A woman called Sally flirts with men while dressed in an extraterrestrial costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name but is a witty remark. 'in' places QUIPMEN inside ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is a general word for kit or apparatus, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Instrument makes woman calcium-deficient

indicators.note: lacking calcium means the woman's name loses those two letters

parts.note: Rebecca is a woman's name
Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium

explanation.surface: A musical instrument leaves a woman short of calcium, as if playing were bad for the bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deficient' strips CA from REBECCA.
explanation.definitionFit: The rebec is a medieval bowed string instrument, an ancestor of the fiddle.

clue.text: State place with enclosures, which has vocalist buzzing

parts.note: KA is a variant abbreviation for the US state of Kansas (usually KS)
a zoo keeps its animals in pens and enclosures

explanation.surface: A walled venue in some state where a singer is humming away.
explanation.walkthrough: KA for Kansas is a rare variant of the usual KS.
explanation.definitionFit: You hum or sing into this toy instrument and its membrane makes the voice buzz.

clue.text: Most rocks, overcoming resistance, cross over house's extra weather protection

indicators.note: the jumble straddles the letter for resistance, sitting over it
rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the letters of most are jumbled

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: in an across clue, over means the word for cross is turned round

parts.note: a rood is a cross, as in a church's rood screen

explanation.surface: Rocks battling resistance and crossing over, like a geology lesson gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' gives STOM, which straddles R; 'over' turns the cross round.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm door is an extra outer door fitted to keep bad weather out of a house.

clue.text: Unmoved, one has to pursue academic success?

indicators.note: following behind means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: a pass is success in an exam
one has contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A calm student who has to chase exam success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one has' is read as the contraction I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmoved and passive both describe someone not reacting or taking action.

clue.text: Knowing about choral arrangement as an academic

indicators.note: the knowing word goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: knowing and sly both mean artful

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks a piece, so choral is rearranged

explanation.surface: An expert on choral arrangements with a scholar's air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' gives CHOLAR; 'Knowing' is an adjective meaning artful.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic as an adjective means learned, bookish, of scholars.

clue.text: Tinker's days standing in line

indicators.note: the two letters stand inside the word for line

parts.note: a file is a line, as in single file
D is the abbreviation for day, so days gives two of them

explanation.surface: A travelling tinker spends days waiting in a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' looks like the mender, but it is the verb, to tinker.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker and to fiddle both mean to fidget with or adjust something idly.

clue.text: Motions not welcomed from her radio broadcast at one

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread and rearranged

parts.note: A means one, as in a single

explanation.surface: Unpopular proposals aired on her radio show at one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motions' looks like debate proposals, but here means bowel movements.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose bowel movements nobody wants is a coy way of describing the condition.

clue.text: Tolls made by regions weather-wise hot, rather than large

indicators.note: the letter for hot takes the place of the letter for large

parts.note: climes are regions considered by their climate
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
H stands for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Bells tolled according to the climate, hot regions over big ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolls are the sounds of bells, as are their chimes.

clue.text: Read superficially, Kipling tale is set in southern sea

indicators.note: the tale is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
Kim is a Rudyard Kipling novel

explanation.surface: A quick skim of a Kipling story set in a southern sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim is to read quickly without taking in the detail.

clue.text: Explicit, grand form of pop with inebriated sound?

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
rap is a style of pop music
hic is the hiccup of a drunk

explanation.surface: Racy lyrics in a big rap track by a drunk-sounding performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphic content is explicit, shown in vivid unsparing detail.

clue.text: President's awards?

definitions.meaning: belonging to Ulysses S Grant, the 18th US president
sums of money given, as for study or research

explanation.definitionFit: Grant was a US president, and allocated funds are another sense of the plural noun.

clue.text: Receiver of beating in eastern temple: bones click, he crumbles

definitions.text: Receiver of beating in eastern temple

indicators.note: something that crumbles falls to bits, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: In an oriental shrine, an old man's bones crack as he collapses under a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beating' suggests violence, but it is drumming.
explanation.definitionFit: This hollow wooden percussion block, also called a temple block, is struck by a player.

clue.text: Bard's exclamation and dash for region of Russia

parts.note: O is a poet's exclamation, as in O for a muse of fire
dash and blast are both mild curses

explanation.surface: Shakespeare cries out and rushes off toward Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' looks like a rush but is an exclamation, like 'blast!'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblast is an administrative province in Russia and other former Soviet states.

clue.text: Wool-producer's call to introduce alkali-treated article with few strings

indicators.note: the bleat takes the jumbled letters into itself

parts.note: a sheep produces wool and its call is baa

indicators.note: chemically treated means the letters of alkali are altered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sheep's bleat prompts a lab to treat an object with alkali.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' gives LALAIK; the definition is 'article with few strings', not just the strings.
explanation.definitionFit: This Russian folk instrument, a thing with only three strings, is described by its sparse stringing.

clue.text: Love to lift and move tongue

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: love is a score of nothing, nil
to go is to move

explanation.surface: A romantic urge to raise and wag one's tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue in the sense of a language; lingo is slang for one.

clue.text: Teacher not quite making a buck?

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a buck is a male rabbit (or hare or deer)

explanation.surface: A teacher who just fails to earn a dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buck' looks like a dollar, but it is the male of the animal; 'not quite' cuts its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher; the Hebrew word means my master.

clue.text: See 20
Personal protection for cutting article

indicators.note: the word for for cuts into the article, splitting it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Safety gear worn when slicing things up.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is worn to protect a person's clothes while cooking or working.

clue.text: Underground mythical treasure guard lacks good ticker

parts.note: the metro is an underground railway

indicators.note: missing the letter for good, so it is taken out

parts.note: gnomes in legend guard underground treasure

explanation.surface: A subterranean treasure-keeping goblin has no good heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ticker' suggests a heart, but it is a device that ticks.
explanation.definitionFit: A metronome ticks steadily to keep time for musicians, so it is a ticker.

clue.text: It's involved with hormones and it's involved with hydro treatment

indicators.note: a treatment works the letters over, so it and hydro are rearranged

parts.note: the pronoun it, the 's being a link and adding no letter

explanation.surface: A spa's water cure is said to act on the body's hormones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' links the second half; 'treatment' rearranges IT and HYDRO.
explanation.definitionFit: The thyroid gland in the neck secretes hormones that regulate metabolism.

clue.text: Crow rig (tension displaced by carbon)

indicators.note: the tension letter is pushed out and the carbon letter put in its place

parts.note: rig and tackle both mean gear, such as fishing tackle
T stands for tension in physics
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A bird-catching contraption rebuilt with carbon parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like the bird, but it is the verb: to gloat noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast or laugh triumphantly, as a cackle does.
